project.domain: fraud operations and deterministic decision support

thesis: The critical fraud decision path is deterministic and evidence-backed; AI is not required to calculate risk or take customer-impacting action.

evidence.claim: Deterministic fraud signals create review cases and the human analyst retains final decision authority.
There is no autonomous agent/tool execution in the critical decision path.
The work sample uses synthetic data and does not claim production banking tenancy.
Human decision retention in the audit trail is part of the behavioral proof.
Source payment events map to deterministic evidence-backed signals and review cases.
Committed behavioral evidence is read by the product proof surface rather than invented by the frontend.
Only synthetic payment/customer data is used; real bank data controls are outside this work sample.
No autonomous LLM/tool loop exists in the decision path.
Evidence, human decision and AuditEntry form a reproducible reviewer-to-engineer proof chain.
No production banking supply-chain assurance claim is made.
The four behavioral evals test correctness and negative cases, not a dedicated security red-team suite.
No production Kafka, bank integration or production monitoring claim is made.

adversarial.taxonomy: No dedicated agentic-security gauntlet; the critical path is deliberately non-agentic

residualRisks: Existing behavioral evals are correctness evidence, not security red-team evidence.
Real bank identity, data-access, transaction-platform and analyst-authorization controls remain outside this synthetic work sample.
If an LLM is later added for explanation or operations, it should remain outside risk scoring and customer-impacting authority unless separately proven.
Production monitoring and incident-response evidence are not claimed.
